# bowang-lab/scgpt (commit cebd6fae655b9c585a4807daa3ac31bb764f06b4)
# bowang-lab/scgpt Overview
scGPT is a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics data. It processes and analyzes complex biological datasets, enabling data management, model training, evaluation, and downstream analysis.

The system incorporates tools for data handling, transforming raw [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects into a standardized format. This includes preprocessing steps like filtering, normalization, and binning of expression values. Data collation mechanisms organize processed data into batches suitable for model input, supporting strategies such as Masked Language Modeling. [Data Management and Preprocessing](#data-management-and-preprocessing) describes these processes.

At its core, [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) uses Transformer architectures designed for single-cell and multi-omic data. These models integrate gene, value, and batch encoding mechanisms to represent biological information. They perform tasks including masked gene modeling, cell-type classification, perturbation prediction, and contrastive learning. [Model Architectures and Training](#model-architectures-and-training) provides further detail.

The models also incorporate adversarial domain adaptation techniques, which mitigate technical batch effects across different datasets or experimental batches. This ensures robustness and generalizability of the learned representations.

Model training follows a workflow that calculates loss functions tailored to specific tasks. The training process includes evaluation procedures that assess model performance and the quality of learned embeddings. [Training and Evaluation Workflow](#introduction-to-scgpt-scgpt-package-structure-and-core-modules-training-and-evaluation-workflow) explains this workflow.

[`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) provides utilities for generating and analyzing embeddings. These embeddings, derived from both cells and genes, serve as representations for downstream analyses like cell clustering, similarity searches, and gene regulatory network inference. [Embedding Generation and Analysis](#embedding-generation-and-analysis) discusses these functionalities.

The system supports fine-tuning pre-trained models on specific datasets or tasks. [Example Workflows and Fine-tuning](#example-workflows-and-fine-tuning) demonstrates this process. Zero-shot capabilities allow application of pre-trained models to new datasets without additional training, for tasks such as reference mapping and data integration. [Zero-Shot Applications and Tutorials](#zero-shot-applications-and-tutorials) provides tutorials on these applications.

## Introduction to scGPT
scGPT is a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics data, leveraging generative AI to process and analyze complex biological datasets. Its capabilities span data management, model training, evaluation, and downstream analysis. The project provides a structured approach to handling single-cell gene expression and multi-omic data, preparing it for input into Transformer-based models.

The system incorporates robust tools for data handling, beginning with preprocessing steps that transform raw [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects into a standardized format. This includes filtering, normalization, log transformation, identification of highly variable genes, and binning of expression values. Data collation mechanisms then organize these processed data points into batches suitable for model input, supporting strategies like Masked Language Modeling (MLM) and custom batch sampling to ensure efficient and flexible data ingestion during training.

At its core, scGPT utilizes sophisticated Transformer architectures designed for single-cell and multi-omic data. These models integrate gene, value, and batch encoding mechanisms to represent biological information effectively. They are capable of performing various tasks, including masked gene modeling, cell-type classification, perturbation prediction, and contrastive learning for self-supervised representation learning. A key feature is the incorporation of adversarial domain adaptation techniques, which help mitigate technical batch effects across different datasets or experimental batches, ensuring the model's robustness and generalizability. These architectures also support optimized attention mechanisms to enhance computational efficiency.

Model training involves a carefully designed workflow that calculates loss functions tailored to specific tasks, such as gene expression prediction and classification. The training process is complemented by comprehensive evaluation procedures that include standard biological metrics, like those provided by [`scib`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L99), and visualization techniques such as UMAP, to assess model performance and the quality of learned embeddings.

Furthermore, scGPT provides utilities for generating and analyzing embeddings. These embeddings, derived from both cells and genes, serve as compact, information-rich representations that can be used for downstream analyses like cell clustering, similarity searches, and gene regulatory network inference. Tools are also available for fine-tuning pre-trained scGPT models on specific datasets or tasks, allowing for adaptation to new biological contexts. For more details on the system's architecture, refer to [scGPT Package Structure and Core Modules](#introduction-to-scgpt-scgpt-package-structure-and-core-modules).

### scGPT Package Structure and Core Modules
The [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) package is organized to facilitate single-cell multi-omics analysis through generative AI. Its primary components are exposed via [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/__init__.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/__init__.py), providing access to core functionalities for data management, model training, evaluation, and analysis.

The package integrates modules for various stages of the workflow:
*   **Model Architectures**: The [`model`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/examples/finetune_integration.py#L385) module in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model) houses the transformer-based models designed for single-cell and multi-omic gene expression data. These architectures support functionalities like gene encoding, value encoding, masked gene modeling, cell-type classification, perturbation prediction, contrastive learning, and adversarial domain adaptation. For more details, refer to [Model Architectures and Training](#model-architectures-and-training).
*   **Tokenization**: The [`tokenizer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/pyproject.toml#L61) module in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer) is responsible for creating, loading, and managing gene vocabularies. It handles the tokenization and padding of gene expression data and adapts to different [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) API versions. Additional information can be found in [Gene Tokenization and Vocabulary](#gene-tokenization-and-vocabulary).
*   **Data Banking**: The [`scbank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/scgpt.rst#L11) module in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank) serves as a structured repository for managing large-scale single-cell RNA-seq datasets, including handling [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, gene tokenization, and metadata management. See [scBank: Structured Data Repository and AnnData Handling](#data-management-and-preprocessing-scbank-structured-data-repository-and-anndata-handling) for further information.
*   **General Utilities**: The [`utils`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L18) module in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/utils`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/utils) provides a collection of utility functions for environment setup, logging, data processing, visualization, model evaluation, and distributed training. Further details are in [Utility Functions and Diagnostics](#utility-functions-and-diagnostics).
*   **Task-Specific Modules**: The [`tasks`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L16) module in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks) provides tools for generating, analyzing, and visualizing gene and cell embeddings from single-cell RNA-seq data, leveraging transformer models and [`scanpy`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L97) for downstream analyses. Refer to [Embedding Generation and Analysis](#embedding-generation-and-analysis) for more information.

Beyond these modules, the package exposes several key classes and functions directly from [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/__init__.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/__init__.py):
*   [`DataCollator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py#L11) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py) is used for batching and preprocessing data for mask value learning tasks, handling padding, truncation, binning, and masking of gene and expression values.
*   [`SubsetsBatchSampler`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_sampler.py#L25) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_sampler.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_sampler.py) provides custom PyTorch [`Sampler`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_sampler.py#L5) implementations for flexible data batching, enabling sampling from multiple distinct data subsets with configurable shuffling.
*   Functions related to the training and evaluation workflow, such as [`prepare_data`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L24), [`prepare_dataloader`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L130), [`train`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L173), [`evaluate`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L379), [`test`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L507), [`define_wandb_metrcis`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L372), and [`eval_testdata`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L589) from [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py), orchestrate the entire learning pipeline, from data preparation to performance metric computation.

The [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) package also handles data preprocessing via the [`Preprocessor`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py#L13) class in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py), which transforms raw single-cell RNA sequencing data into a format suitable for various models. Masked loss functions are defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/loss.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/loss.py) to compare model outputs with targets, ignoring specific elements based on a mask.

#### Data Preparation and Batching Mechanisms
The data preparation and batching mechanisms within [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) are designed to transform raw single-cell RNA sequencing data into a format suitable for transformer-based models, facilitating tasks such as Masked Language Modeling (MLM). This process involves a series of steps, from initial preprocessing to custom batch sampling and data collation.

Data preprocessing is handled by the [`Preprocessor`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py#L13) class in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py). This class orchestrates common steps for [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, including filtering genes and cells based on expression counts, normalizing total counts, applying [`log1p`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py#L26) transformation, selecting highly variable genes, and binning continuous expression values. Binning converts continuous data into discrete categories, which can be useful for tokenization in models that expect discrete inputs. The [`Preprocessor`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/preprocess.py#L13) ensures that data is consistently formatted and cleaned before further processing.

Following preprocessing, the [`DataCollator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py#L11) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py) plays a central role in preparing batches for model input, particularly for tasks like MLM. This component manages padding and truncation of gene and expression sequences to uniform lengths, ensuring compatibility with fixed-size model inputs. For MLM tasks, it intelligently masks a percentage of expression values, replacing them with a designated [`mask_value`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py#L43), which enables the model to learn context by predicting these masked values. The [`DataCollator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py#L11) also supports binning expressions if configured, further discretizing values. It ensures that special tokens, typically located at the beginning of a sequence, are preserved from masking or sampling.

For flexible data loading and training, [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) employs custom batch sampling strategies defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_sampler.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_sampler.py). The [`SubsetsBatchSampler`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_sampler.py#L25) allows for the creation of batches from multiple distinct subsets of data indices. This is particularly useful in scenarios where a dataset might be partitioned (e.g., by cell type or experimental batch) and there's a need to sample batches either sequentially or randomly from these partitions. It supports both intra-subset shuffling (shuffling indices within each partition) and inter-subset shuffling (randomizing the order in which batches are drawn from different partitions), providing fine-grained control over the batching process to optimize training dynamics.

#### Training and Evaluation Workflow
The [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) repository orchestrates the end-to-end process of training, evaluating, and applying single-cell GPT models, encompassing data preparation for diverse tasks, iterative training loops with various loss functions, validation on held-out sets, and comprehensive performance assessment.

The workflow begins with data preparation, managed by [`prepare_data`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L24) within [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py). This function preprocesses tokenized gene expression data, applying masking strategies for denoising or prediction tasks. It structures the data into dictionaries suitable for both training and validation, accommodating different biological tasks such as cell type annotation, multi-batch integration, perturbation prediction, and multi-omic analysis. For optimal training efficiency, it can also sort sequences by batch, which is beneficial when utilizing specialized data samplers.

Data is then loaded using the [`SeqDataset`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L118) class and [`prepare_dataloader`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L130) function from [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py). These components facilitate the creation of [`DataLoader`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L4) instances, which can either shuffle data conventionally or employ a custom batch sampling strategy. This strategy groups samples from the same "sequence batch" to ensure that each training batch contains related data, thereby potentially improving learning dynamics.

The core training process is executed by the [`train`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L173) function in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py). This function performs forward passes through the model and calculates various loss components. These components can include Gene Expression Prediction (GEP), Gene Expression Prediction with Cell Embeddings (GEPC), Cell-type Classification (CLS), Entropy-based Contrastive Learning (ECS), and Discriminative Adversarial Batch (DAR) losses. The integration of these diverse loss functions allows the model to learn from multiple aspects of single-cell data simultaneously. Model weights are updated using an optimizer and scheduler, and mixed-precision training is enabled through [`torch.cuda.amp.autocast`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L220) for enhanced performance and reduced memory footprint. Detailed training metrics are logged to [`wandb`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L40) for monitoring progress.

During training, model performance is regularly assessed on a validation set by the [`evaluate`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L379) function in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py). This function operates without weight updates, focusing solely on calculating the relevant loss for the specific task at hand (e.g., CLS loss for annotation tasks or GEP loss for integration tasks).

For comprehensive performance evaluation, particularly for classification tasks, the [`predict`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L463) and [`test`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L507) functions in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py) are utilized. [`predict`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L463) generates classification labels from input data, while [`test`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L507) processes raw [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, tokenizes them, and then uses [`predict`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L463) to derive predictions. It subsequently calculates and logs classification performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

A specialized evaluation function, [`eval_testdata`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L589) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py), focuses on assessing the quality of cell embeddings. It uses the trained model to generate cell embeddings, stores them in the [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) object, and then leverages [`scib`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L99) metrics to quantify biological conservation and batch integration performance. This function also generates UMAP visualizations, offering a visual assessment of batch and cell-type integration, complementing the quantitative metrics. The various masked loss functions used during training are defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/loss.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/loss.py).

## Data Management and Preprocessing
The [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) project employs a robust data management system to process large-scale single-cell and multi-omic gene expression datasets. This system encompasses data access, pretraining, annotation, integration, perturbation prediction, gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis, and zero-shot integration. It is designed to handle [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects and organize datasets into a structured repository.

A central aspect of [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1)'s data management involves building a pre-training cell corpus from the Cellxgene Census. This process includes defining queries, indexing [`soma_joinid`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L37)s, chunked downloading of data, converting data to the [`scb`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L49) format, and parallel processing using SLURM for efficient, large-scale data ingestion. The pipeline also supports advanced filtering mechanisms, such as filtering for specific cancer types.

The primary datasets used in the [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) manuscript are organized within the [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data) directory. This includes pretraining data, as well as datasets tailored for cell type annotation, multi-batch and multi-omics integration, perturbation prediction, GRN analysis, and zero-shot integration. The [`README.md`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/pyproject.toml#L9) file within this directory provides a comprehensive guide to accessing these processed datasets, often linking to external resources.

For managing these datasets, [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) utilizes [`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45), a structured data repository. This module facilitates the efficient import of [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, tokenization of gene expression data, management of metadata, and persistence of data to disk in the [`scb`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L49) format. The [`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45) core components are defined within the [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank) directory.

The [`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45) system is built around the [`DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L19) class, which acts as a central repository for multi-study single-cell data. It manages [`MetaInfo`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L43) (metadata), [`DataTable`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L11) objects, [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) for gene tokenization, and [`Setting`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/setting.py#L7) objects for configuration. The [`DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L19) supports importing data directly from [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, tokenizing gene expression data, and persisting these processed data to disk. It handles [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) layers and observations, converting them into [`DataTable`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L11)s and ensuring token matching with the gene vocabulary. For large datasets, the [`DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L19) is designed to store data chunks on disk and load partitions into memory as needed, optimizing memory usage. It also automatically converts dense NumPy arrays to sparse [`csr_matrix`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L8) where appropriate to enhance memory and processing efficiency for typical biological data.

### Cellxgene Census Data Ingestion Pipeline
The Cellxgene Census Data Ingestion Pipeline automates the construction of a pre-training cell corpus from the Cellxgene Census, designed to support large-scale machine learning model development. This pipeline is optimized for cluster environments leveraging SLURM for parallel processing. The process begins with configuring specific data queries, proceeds through indexing cell identifiers, downloading data in manageable chunks, converting the data into an efficient [`scb`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L49) format, and includes advanced filtering capabilities for specific cancer types and organs.

A core aspect of the pipeline is its configuration for data queries, primarily defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py). This file establishes constants such as [`MAJOR_TISSUE_LIST`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L4), [`VERSION`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L5) for the Cellxgene Census, and the path to [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/cancer_list.txt`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/cancer_list.txt), which enumerates cancer types. These definitions are used to construct SQL-like filter strings in [`VALUE_FILTER`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L12) for querying normal tissue samples, "other" tissues not explicitly listed, and pan-cancer datasets based on disease types. The [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/query_list.txt`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/query_list.txt) file further specifies human organs and conditions for targeting data retrieval.

Once queries are defined, the pipeline indexes cell identifiers. The [`soma_joinid`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L37)s, which are unique Cellxgene Census identifiers, are retrieved based on the specified queries. This is managed by [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py), which uses [`retrieve_soma_idx`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L29) to query the census and [`convert2file`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L43) to save these identifiers into [`.idx`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L51) files. The shell script [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.sh`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.sh) orchestrates this indexing for multiple queries. For further details on this process, see [Cell Indexing and Query Definition](#data-management-and-preprocessing-cellxgene-census-data-ingestion-pipeline-cell-indexing-and-query-definition).

For efficient handling of large datasets, the pipeline employs a chunked data downloading strategy. [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py) facilitates downloading specific partitions of Homo sapiens data from the Cellxgene Census as [`h5ad`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L14) files. It leverages [`load2list`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py#L60) to read SOMA IDs, [`define_partition`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py#L50) to select a subset of IDs, and [`download_partition`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py#L70) to execute the query and save the [`anndata`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) object. The [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/array_download_partition.sh`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/array_download_partition.sh) script utilizes SLURM array jobs to parallelize these chunked downloads, ensuring efficient retrieval of vast quantities of data. More information can be found in [Chunked Data Downloading and SLURM Parallelization](#data-management-and-preprocessing-cellxgene-census-data-ingestion-pipeline-chunked-data-downloading-and-slurm-parallelization).

Following the download, the [`h5ad`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L14) files are converted into the [`scb`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L49) (single-cell bank) format, which is optimized for high-performance I/O in downstream machine learning tasks. This conversion is handled by [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_large_scale_data.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_large_scale_data.py), which preprocesses [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, filtering cells and genes as needed, and then converts them into [`scbank.DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_large_scale_data.py#L190) objects. The [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/array_build_scb.sh`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/array_build_scb.sh) script orchestrates this conversion process across multiple datasets using SLURM array jobs.

The pipeline also includes mechanisms for gene vocabulary expansion and data processing for model training. [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/expand_gene_list.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/expand_gene_list.py) updates the gene vocabulary by incorporating new gene symbols from the Cellxgene Census. Finally, [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/process_allcounts.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/process_allcounts.py) configures and preprocesses single-cell gene expression data for transformer model training, loading vocabularies and appending special tokens like [`"<cls>"`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L529). This comprehensive approach ensures that vast amounts of single-cell data are efficiently prepared for advanced analysis and model training.

#### Cell Indexing and Query Definition
The process of defining queries and indexing [`soma_joinid`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L37)s from the Cellxgene Census begins with the configuration of data queries. This involves setting up constants such as [`MAJOR_TISSUE_LIST`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L4), [`VERSION`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L5), and [`CANCER_LIST_PATH`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L7) within [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py). This file programmatically constructs SQL-like filter strings stored in [`VALUE_FILTER`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L12) for querying normal tissue samples, specific "other" tissues, and [`pan-cancer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L69) datasets based on disease lists. The [`CANCER_LIST_PATH`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L7) points to [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/cancer_list.txt`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/cancer_list.txt), which enumerates various cancer types used to build the [`pan-cancer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L69) filter. [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/query_list.txt`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/query_list.txt) further specifies predefined human organs and conditions for querying.

Once queries are defined, the system proceeds to cell indexing. The script [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py) is responsible for retrieving [`soma_joinid`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L37)s (unique Cellxgene Census identifiers). It queries the Cellxgene Census using [`cellxgene_census.open_soma`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L34) and the [`VALUE_FILTER`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py#L12) from [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/data_config.py). These identifiers are then saved to [`.idx`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L51) files for efficient data access, with the process orchestrated by [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.sh`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.sh). This step ensures that specific cell populations can be precisely identified and retrieved for subsequent data processing.

#### Chunked Data Downloading and SLURM Parallelization
To manage the download of large datasets from the Cellxgene Census, [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) employs a strategy of chunked data downloading and parallel processing. This approach prevents memory overload and ensures efficient data retrieval.

The script [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py) is central to this process. It downloads specific partitions of [`Homo sapiens`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py#L79) data from the Cellxgene Census, saving them as [`h5ad`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L14) files. The process involves identifying a list of SOMA IDs (unique Cellxgene Census identifiers) using [`load2list`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py#L60) and then selecting a subset of these IDs to form a manageable chunk using [`define_partition`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py#L50). This enables the retrieval of an [`anndata`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) object from the [`cellxgene_census`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/build_soma_idx.py#L3), which is then saved to disk. A related function, [`del_partition`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.py#L90), allows for the removal of previously downloaded partition files.

For parallel execution, especially in cluster environments, [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) utilizes SLURM array jobs through the script [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/array_download_partition.sh`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/array_download_partition.sh). This shell script orchestrates the downloading of data partitions by defining SLURM parameters such as time, CPU, and memory allocation. It leverages the [`SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/array_build_scb.sh#L13) to iterate through a list of queries defined in [`QUERY_PATH`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L29), executing [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.sh`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/download_partition.sh) for each partition. This mechanism ensures that different parts of the dataset can be downloaded concurrently, significantly speeding up the overall data acquisition process.

### scBank: Structured Data Repository and AnnData Handling
The [`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45) module provides a structured repository for managing large-scale single-cell RNA-seq datasets, designed to streamline data handling from import to persistence. The core of this system is the [`DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L19) class, which serves as a central hub for organizing multi-study single-cell data. It manages metadata, stores data tables, handles gene tokenization, and applies configuration settings.

Data within [`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45) is represented using [`DataTable`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L11) objects, which encapsulate individual data tables with names and associated [`Dataset`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py#L64) objects. Metadata for an entire [`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45) data directory is managed by the [`MetaInfo`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L43) class, tracking essential information such as on-disk path, data format, main data table key, and gene vocabulary checksum. This structured approach facilitates efficient data access and management.

A key capability of [`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45) is its integration with [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, a common format in single-cell genomics. The [`DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L19) can import data directly from [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects or their file paths, tokenizing gene expression data as part of this process. This tokenization is critical for downstream machine learning tasks, as it converts gene names into numerical identifiers using a [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) object. For large datasets, the system can tokenize data from specific layers or observations within an [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) object, ensuring efficient memory usage.

[`scBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L45) is also designed for data persistence and synchronization. Changes to the [`DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L19) can be tracked and then synchronized to disk, saving metadata, data tables (typically in [`scb`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/data/cellxgene/README.md#L49) format), and the gene vocabulary. While a full [`save`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/data.py#L23) mechanism is planned for future development, the current [`sync`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L634) functionality supports managing data on disk. Configuration settings, defined by the [`Setting`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/setting.py#L7) dataclass in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/setting.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/setting.py), allow customization of [`DataBank`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/scbank/databank.py#L19) behavior, such as removing zero rows during data loading or controlling immediate saving to disk. The overall design emphasizes managing large datasets by storing data chunks on disk and providing mechanisms to load relevant partitions as needed, as indicated by placeholder methods for large-scale data handling.

## Gene Tokenization and Vocabulary
[`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) manages gene vocabularies for single-cell gene expression data, which involves creating, loading, and applying these vocabularies to convert gene expression measurements into tokenized representations suitable for transformer models. This process ensures that gene expression data can be uniformly processed and fed into models, regardless of variations in the input data. The system dynamically adapts to changes in the [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) API, maintaining compatibility across different [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) versions.

The core of this system is defined in the [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer) directory, which provides functionalities for vocabulary management and data processing. The [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) class, found in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py), is central to this. It handles the initialization of vocabularies from various sources, including lists of gene names or existing vocabulary objects. [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) also supports loading and saving vocabularies to files, such as [`.pkl`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L120) or [`.json`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/utils/util.py#L223) formats, for persistence and reuse. It incorporates mechanisms for managing special tokens (e.g., for padding or classification) and for setting a default token. For instance, the [`pad_token`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L201) property ensures proper padding within batches. A [`get_default_gene_vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L242) function is available to retrieve or construct a standard gene vocabulary, potentially fetching gene symbols from external sources like [`genenames.org`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L274).

Beyond vocabulary creation, the system includes utilities for tokenizing and padding gene expression data. Functions like [`tokenize_batch`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L292) convert numerical gene expression values and identifiers into tokenized representations, often including special tokens like a [`cls_id`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L298) (classification token). [`pad_batch`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L355) then takes these tokenized batches and pads them to a uniform length ([`max_len`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L525)) using a specified [`pad_token`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L201) and [`pad_value`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py#L39), ensuring that all input sequences to the model have consistent dimensions. If a batch item exceeds the maximum length, genes are sampled to fit the constraint while preserving critical tokens. The [`tokenize_and_pad_batch`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L442) utility combines these steps for a streamlined workflow. Additionally, [`random_mask_value`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L485) facilitates tasks such as Masked Language Modeling by randomly masking a proportion of gene expression values in a batch, excluding padding values.

A crucial aspect of [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1)'s gene tokenization system is its adaptability to [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) API changes, as handled by [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py). This module dynamically probes whether [`torchtext.vocab.Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L14) can be subclassed. If it cannot (a common issue with newer [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) versions), the system gracefully falls back to a pure-Python [`BuiltinVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L81) implementation. This [`BuiltinVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L81) mirrors the public API of [`torchtext.vocab.Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L14), providing a consistent interface for [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) regardless of the underlying [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) version. This design ensures that [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) remains robust against external library updates while maintaining its core functionality for gene tokenization.

### GeneVocab Class: Core Vocabulary Management
The [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) class, defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py), is central to managing gene vocabularies within scGPT. It extends a base [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) class, which is dynamically selected based on [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) compatibility to ensure consistent functionality across different versions. See [Dynamic Vocab Compatibility and `torchtext` Adaptation](#gene-tokenization-and-vocabulary-dynamic-vocab-compatibility-and-torchtext-adaptation) for details on this dynamic compatibility.

[`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) can be initialized from various sources: a list of gene names, an existing [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) object, or a [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) vocabulary. This flexibility allows for diverse vocabulary construction scenarios. During initialization, it handles special tokens, such as padding tokens, and can set a default token for out-of-vocabulary terms. The class includes mechanisms for persistent storage and retrieval of vocabularies, offering [`from_file`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L113) methods to load from [`.pkl`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L120) or [`.json`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/utils/util.py#L223) files and [`save_json`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L221) to write vocabularies to JSON format. This enables efficient reuse of pre-built vocabularies without needing to reconstruct them every time.

A default gene vocabulary can be automatically built or retrieved using the [`get_default_gene_vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L242) function. This function attempts to load a default vocabulary from a predefined JSON file. If no such file exists, it constructs the vocabulary by fetching gene symbols and IDs from [`genenames.org`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L274) and then saves it for future use. This provides a standardized and readily available vocabulary for common use cases. The [`pad_token`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L201) property specifically manages the padding token, ensuring its presence within the vocabulary for proper batching operations.

### Dynamic Vocab Compatibility and `torchtext` Adaptation
The [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) project maintains compatibility with varying [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) API versions through the [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py) module. This module addresses changes in [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) where [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) became a non-subclassable C++ extension in versions 0.14 and later, which impacts the ability to extend its functionality.

To ensure a consistent [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) interface regardless of the [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) version, [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) dynamically checks if [`torchtext.vocab.Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L14) can be subclassed. This check is performed by [`_probe_torchtext_vocab_subclassable`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L36). If it can, the system leverages the native [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) [`Vocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L251) class. If not, a pure-Python fallback implementation named [`BuiltinVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L81) is used instead. This [`BuiltinVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/vocab_compat.py#L81) class provides a compatible public API for token-to-index and index-to-token mappings, handling out-of-vocabulary tokens, and supporting token manipulation. This approach allows the [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) class to operate seamlessly across different [`torchtext`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/environment.yml#L19) environments without requiring modifications to its core logic, thereby maintaining stability and flexibility in vocabulary management. Further details on [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) can be found in [GeneVocab Class: Core Vocabulary Management](#gene-tokenization-and-vocabulary-genevocab-class-core-vocabulary-management).

### Tokenization, Padding, and Masking Utilities
The [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) project employs several utility functions to prepare gene expression data for transformer models, covering tokenization, padding, and masking, primarily defined within [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py).

Gene expression data, initially represented by numerical counts and gene identifiers, is converted into a tokenized format suitable for sequence models. The [`tokenize_batch`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L292) function performs this conversion by transforming non-zero gene expressions into a list of tuples, each containing a gene identifier and its corresponding expression count. Optionally, a [`cls_id`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L298) can be appended to these tokenized representations, serving as a special classification token.

Once tokenized, gene batches are uniformly sized through padding, which is handled by the [`pad_batch`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L355) function. This function extends shorter sequences to a [`max_len`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L525) using a specified [`pad_token`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L201) and [`pad_value`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py#L39). If a sequence exceeds [`max_len`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L525), genes are sampled to fit the target length, ensuring that the optional [`cls_appended`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L361) token remains at the beginning of the sequence. The [`tokenize_and_pad_batch`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L442) function combines these tokenization and padding steps into a single, streamlined process.

For tasks such as Masked Language Modeling (MLM), [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) incorporates a masking mechanism. The [`random_mask_value`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L485) function applies masking to a random subset of gene expression values within a batch. Based on a defined [`mask_ratio`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/examples/finetune_integration.py#L89), selected values are replaced with a [`mask_value`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/data_collator.py#L43), while padding values are explicitly excluded from this process. This allows the model to learn to predict missing gene expressions based on context. For further details on the [`GeneVocab`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py#L24) class which manages the underlying vocabulary, see [GeneVocab Class: Core Vocabulary Management](#gene-tokenization-and-vocabulary-genevocab-class-core-vocabulary-management).

## Model Architectures and Training
scGPT employs transformer-based models designed to process single-cell and multi-omic gene expression data, supporting a range of functionalities from data encoding to various prediction and integration tasks. The primary implementations reside in the [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model) directory.

The system utilizes specialized encoders, such as [`GeneEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L717), [`ContinuousValueEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L759), [`CategoryValueEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L789), and [`BatchLabelEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L809), to convert raw gene identifiers, continuous expression values, categorical values, and batch labels into dense embeddings suitable for transformer input. These embeddings are then processed by a transformer encoder, which can be configured to use standard PyTorch implementations or optimized attention mechanisms for computational efficiency, such as those provided by [`FlashTransformerEncoderLayer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L588) and [`FastTransformerEncoderWrapper`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L500). For details on the dynamic compatibility with [`flash-attn`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L18) backends, see [Optimized Attention Mechanisms](#model-architectures-and-training-optimized-attention-mechanisms).

The core model, [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), supports various training objectives:
*   **Masked Gene Modeling:** Predicts masked gene expression values using an [`ExprDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L842).
*   **Cell-Type Classification:** Classifies cell types based on cell embeddings via a [`ClsDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L884).
*   **Contrastive Learning:** Uses objectives like Contrastive Cell Embedding (CCE) and Elastic Cell Similarity (ECS) to learn robust cell representations by maximizing agreement between related embeddings.
*   **Adversarial Domain Adaptation:** Integrates an [`AdversarialDiscriminator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L1007) with a [`grad_reverse`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py#L16) mechanism to mitigate batch effects and learn domain-invariant features. This process helps ensure that cell embeddings are comparable across different experimental batches or datasets. The [`DomainSpecificBatchNorm1d`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py#L63) module in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py) further assists in batch effect correction by maintaining separate batch normalization statistics for different domains.

For multi-omic datasets, the [`MultiOmicTransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py#L21) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py) extends these capabilities, enabling the integration and analysis of diverse data types. It shares many architectural components with the [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21), adapting them for multi-omic input and tasks.

The [`TransformerGenerator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L27) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py) is specifically designed for generative tasks, including masked gene modeling and perturbation prediction. It incorporates a [`pert_encoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L80) to embed perturbation flags and utilizes an [`AffineExprDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L373) to predict both baseline gene expression and the effects of perturbations.

Model training involves feeding these encoded inputs through the transformer, computing task-specific losses (e.g., MLM loss, classification loss, adversarial loss), and optimizing the model parameters. Evaluation often includes metrics from [`scib`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L99) and visualization techniques like UMAP to assess the quality of cell embeddings and batch correction. For a deeper understanding of the loss functions, refer to [Training and Evaluation Workflow](#introduction-to-scgpt-scgpt-package-structure-and-core-modules-training-and-evaluation-workflow).

### Transformer Model Architectures for Single-Cell Data
scGPT utilizes transformer-based architectures to process single-cell and multi-omic gene expression data. The primary models, [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21) and [`MultiOmicTransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py#L21), are designed to integrate gene, value, and batch information to support various analytical tasks.

The [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21), defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), processes single-cell gene expression data by first encoding gene identifiers, continuous expression values, and optional batch labels into a combined embedding space. These embeddings are then fed into a Transformer encoder, which can be configured to use standard, fast, or [`FlashTransformerEncoderLayer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L588) attention mechanisms for optimized computational efficiency. The model supports multiple objectives including Masked Language Modeling (MLM) for predicting gene expression, cell-type classification (CLS), Contrastive Cell Embedding (CCE) for self-supervised learning, and adversarial domain adaptation (DAB) to correct for batch effects.

For datasets comprising multiple omics layers, the [`MultiOmicTransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py#L21), located in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py), extends this architecture. It similarly encodes gene, value, and batch information, alongside modality types, and processes them through a Transformer encoder. This model supports the same diverse range of tasks as the [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21), including MLM, CLS, CCE, and DAB, ensuring its applicability across complex multi-omic data. Both models utilize [`DomainSpecificBatchNorm1d`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py#L63) from [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py) and a [`grad_reverse`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py#L16) layer from [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py) to facilitate adversarial training for batch effect correction.

To enhance computational efficiency, both models integrate optimized attention mechanisms. This includes [`FlashTransformerEncoderLayer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L588) and [`FastTransformerEncoderWrapper`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L500), which utilize high-performance Flash attention backends or linear attention techniques. Compatibility with different versions of the [`flash-attn`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L18) library is managed through [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/flash_attn_compat.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/flash_attn_compat.py), which provides a unified interface and handles dynamic loading of available backends. For a detailed explanation of Flash-Attention diagnostics, see [Flash-Attention Diagnostics and Troubleshooting](#utility-functions-and-diagnostics-flash-attention-diagnostics-and-troubleshooting).

The overall structure of these models, including their various encoders, decoders, and specialized layers, is aggregated and exposed through [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/__init__.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/__init__.py), streamlining their integration into broader workflows within the scGPT framework.

### Generative Models and Perturbation Prediction
The [`TransformerGenerator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L27) model, primarily defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py), is designed for generative tasks within single-cell gene expression data, focusing on masked gene modeling and the prediction of perturbation effects. This model extends the core transformer architecture to address tasks beyond simple classification or embedding generation.

The [`TransformerGenerator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L27) integrates a [`GeneEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L717) for gene embeddings, a [`ContinuousValueEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L759) for expression values, and a unique [`pert_encoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L80) for handling perturbation flags. These components feed into a transformer encoder, similar to other models within the scGPT framework, but the distinguishing features lie in its decoders and specialized methods.

For predicting gene expression values, the model employs an [`AffineExprDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L373), which is specifically designed to output gene expression values and can optionally model explicit zero probabilities, a common characteristic of single-cell RNA sequencing data. This decoder can also predict perturbation effects, allowing the model to simulate how gene expression might change under different experimental conditions. The [`pred_perturb`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L292) method within [`TransformerGenerator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L27) is dedicated to this task, enabling dynamic selection of genes and mapping them to vocabulary IDs for perturbation prediction.

Beyond expression prediction, the [`TransformerGenerator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L27) also supports cell-type classification via a [`ClsDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L884) and masked value prediction with an [`MVCDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L915), demonstrating its multi-task capabilities within a generative framework. The model's design emphasizes modularity, allowing for flexible configuration of encoders and decoders, and integrates fast transformer backends for computational efficiency, particularly when handling large datasets.

### Encoding and Decoding Mechanisms
The [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) repository utilizes a modular approach for processing single-cell and multi-omic gene expression data, employing a suite of encoding and decoding mechanisms. These modules transform raw biological data into a format suitable for transformer models and then interpret the model's output back into meaningful biological predictions.

### Encoders

The encoding modules convert different types of input data into dense numerical representations (embeddings) that the transformer models can process.

*   **[`GeneEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L717)**: This module, found in files such as [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), maps discrete gene identifiers into continuous vector embeddings. This is analogous to word embeddings in natural language processing, where each gene is assigned a unique vector that captures its characteristics within the biological context. A [`nn.LayerNorm`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L645) is applied after the embedding for normalization.
*   **[`ContinuousValueEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L759)**: Located in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), this encoder transforms continuous numerical values, such as gene expression levels, into embeddings. It typically uses multiple [`nn.Linear`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L641) layers with [`nn.ReLU`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L768) activations and [`nn.LayerNorm`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L645) to process these values, optionally clipping input values to a maximum range.
*   **[`CategoryValueEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L789)**: Also defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), this module is used for categorical numerical values, such as binned gene expression values. Similar to [`GeneEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L717), it uses [`nn.Embedding`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L725) to map these categories to vectors.
*   **[`BatchLabelEncoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L809)**: In [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), this encoder handles batch or modality labels, converting them into embeddings. This allows the model to incorporate information about the origin or type of data sample, which can be crucial for mitigating technical variations (batch effects).
*   **[`pert_encoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L80)**: Specifically used in generative models like [`TransformerGenerator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L27) in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py), this encoder embeds perturbation flags. These flags indicate whether a cell or gene has undergone a specific perturbation (e.g., control, drug treatment), enabling the model to learn and predict the effects of such interventions.

### Decoders

The decoding modules interpret the transformer model's processed embeddings to generate specific predictions or outputs related to the biological tasks.

*   **[`ExprDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L842)**: Found in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), this decoder is responsible for predicting gene expression values. It takes the transformer's output and uses a multi-layer perceptron ([`self.fc`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L851)) to estimate expression. It can also model an explicit zero probability ([`self.zero_logit`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L860)), which is important for handling the sparsity common in single-cell gene expression data.
*   **[`AffineExprDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py#L373)**: Defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/generation_model.py), this is a specialized expression decoder used in generative models. It predicts gene expression values using an affine transformation of the form [`Ax + b`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/utils/util.py#L93), where [`A`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/LICENSE#L17) and [`b`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/docs/make.bat#L23) are generated by internal [`ExprDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L842) instances. This allows for more flexible and interpretable modeling of gene expression, including handling explicit zero probabilities and adaptive biases.
*   **[`ClsDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L884)**: In [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), this decoder performs classification tasks, typically for cell types. It uses an MLP with [`nn.Linear`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L641) layers and [`nn.LayerNorm`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L645) to map a cell-level embedding (derived from the transformer's output) to a probability distribution over predefined cell classes.
*   **[`MVCDecoder`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L915)**: This decoder, located in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py), handles Masked Value Prediction. It combines cell and gene embeddings to predict values that were masked during training. It supports various architectural styles (e.g., "inner product", "concat query", "sum query") for combining these embeddings and can also predict explicit zero probabilities.

### Adversarial Domain Adaptation and Batch Effect Correction
Adversarial domain adaptation is implemented within scGPT models to mitigate batch effects and enhance generalization across different datasets or experimental batches. This is achieved through a combination of techniques, primarily leveraging gradient reversal layers and domain-specific batch normalization.

The core mechanism involves an [`AdversarialDiscriminator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L1007), typically integrated into the [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21) and [`MultiOmicTransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py#L21) architectures found in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py) and [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py). This discriminator works in an adversarial fashion: the main feature extractor (the Transformer encoder) attempts to learn features that are indistinguishable across domains, while the discriminator tries to correctly classify the domain of origin for a given cell embedding. This adversarial objective encourages the model to learn domain-invariant representations.

A crucial component enabling this adversarial training is the [`grad_reverse`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py#L16) mechanism, which is defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py). This layer reverses the gradient flow during backpropagation, meaning that gradients passing through it have their signs flipped. When used between the feature extractor and the discriminator, it ensures that the feature extractor is trained to *confuse* the discriminator about the domain of origin, thereby producing features that are less specific to any single batch or domain.

Further contributing to batch effect correction is [`DomainSpecificBatchNorm1d`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py#L63), implemented in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py). Unlike standard batch normalization which computes statistics across all data in a batch, [`DomainSpecificBatchNorm1d`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py#L63) maintains separate normalization parameters and statistics for each domain (e.g., each batch or dataset). During the forward pass, the appropriate batch normalization layer is selected based on the input's domain label. This ensures that features are normalized within their respective domains, preventing inter-domain statistical shifts from compromising model performance and leading to more robust, batch-effect-corrected embeddings.

Together, the [`AdversarialDiscriminator`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L1007) with [`grad_reverse`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/grad_reverse.py#L16) and [`DomainSpecificBatchNorm1d`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/dsbn.py#L63) provide a robust framework within scGPT for learning features that are less sensitive to technical variations introduced by different experimental batches, thus improving the generalizability and utility of the learned representations for diverse single-cell and multi-omic datasets. For further details on the Transformer models that integrate these components, refer to [Transformer Model Architectures for Single-Cell Data](#model-architectures-and-training-transformer-model-architectures-for-single-cell-data).

### Optimized Attention Mechanisms
[`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) incorporates optimized attention mechanisms to enhance the computational efficiency of its transformer models, particularly when processing long gene sequences. This is achieved through the integration of [`FlashTransformerEncoderLayer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L588) and [`FastTransformerEncoderWrapper`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L500), which leverage specialized libraries for faster attention computations.

The [`FlashTransformerEncoderLayer`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L588) allows the transformer to utilize FlashAttention, a technique that significantly speeds up attention calculations by reducing memory I/O and increasing throughput. Its compatibility is managed by [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/flash_attn_compat.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/flash_attn_compat.py), which provides a unified [`FlashMHA`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/flash_attn_compat.py#L75) API that dynamically loads either [`flash-attn`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L18) version 1.x or 2.x based on availability, with a preference for 1.x for its simpler API. This compatibility layer also includes utilities for detecting [`flash-attn`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L18) availability and handling parameter naming inconsistencies in model checkpoints, ensuring seamless integration and model loading.

Alternatively, [`scGPT`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L1) can employ [`FastTransformerEncoderWrapper`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L500), which interfaces with the [`fast_transformers`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L518) library to use linear attention. This provides another efficient alternative to standard quadratic attention mechanisms, offering performance benefits. These optimized layers are integrated into the core transformer architectures, including the [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21) and [`MultiOmicTransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/multiomic_model.py#L21), enabling them to process single-cell and multi-omic data more efficiently across various tasks. The choice between standard, Flash, or linear attention can be configured to balance computational speed with model complexity and available hardware resources.

## Embedding Generation and Analysis
scGPT provides functionalities for generating, analyzing, and visualizing gene and cell embeddings from single-cell RNA-seq data, leveraging transformer models and [`scanpy`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L97) for downstream analyses. The primary components for these tasks are exposed through [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks).

Cell embeddings are generated from single-cell RNA-seq data using a pre-trained [`TransformerModel`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/model/model.py#L21). The [`embed_data`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py#L148) function within [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py) orchestrates this process, loading a model and its associated vocabulary, preprocessing [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects to match genes with the model's vocabulary, and then computing embeddings. The [`get_batch_cell_embeddings`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py#L22) function handles the batch processing of [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, transforming gene expression profiles into dense, numerical representations. These embeddings, typically derived from the model's [`<cls>`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L529) token output, can be used for various downstream analyses.

For gene embeddings, the [`GeneEmbedding`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/grn.py#L18) class, defined in [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/grn.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/grn.py), manages gene embeddings and provides tools for their analysis and visualization. It initializes with gene names and their corresponding embedding vectors, which can be loaded from files. The system can convert these gene embeddings into a [`scanpy`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/README.md#L97) [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) object, allowing for standard analyses such as neighborhood graph construction, Leiden clustering, and UMAP dimensionality reduction. This enables the visualization of gene clusters, referred to as metagenes. Furthermore, [`GeneEmbedding`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/grn.py#L18) facilitates the computation and plotting of gene similarities using cosine similarity, the scoring of metagenes within [`AnnData`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/trainer.py#L9) objects, and the construction of gene similarity networks using [`networkx`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/grn.py#L7). These tools support the investigation of gene relationships and the impact of specific gene sets.

### Cell Embedding Generation and Preprocessing
The generation of cell embeddings from single-cell RNA-seq data is a core capability within scGPT, enabling the transformation of high-dimensional gene expression profiles into a lower-dimensional, dense numerical representation. This process facilitates downstream analyses such as clustering, visualization, and cell type annotation. The primary tools for this task are found within [`/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py`](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scgpt/scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py).
